This is the UK's proposed plan for what we are calling the New European Union, or NEU:

Changes

  • Immigration policy will be independently controlled by member states. This does not apply to the Schengen Area, and any citizen of the NEU will be able to move freely between countries.

  • NEU sanctions and embargoes will not be decided by any NEU organisation. Instead, member states will vote on NEU-wide sanctions and embargoes, with a majority of nations' votes being the deciding factor in them being applied. When entered into action, they will be enforced by the Customs Union, who will work directly with governmental organisations of member states.

  • Article 17 of the treaty of the European Union will be changed. The article basically outlines the responsibilities of the European Commission, which is the branch that drafts legislature. Each member state gets to elect their own commissioner, then a president is elected out of all the commissioners. The article includes this section:

In carrying out its responsibilities, the Commission shall be completely independent. Without prejudice to Article 18(2), the members of the Commission shall neither seek nor take instructions from any Government or other institution, body, office or entity. They shall refrain from any action incompatible with their duties or the performance of their tasks.

This will be revoked. The duty of the NEU Commission will be to represent their countries when legislature is drafted. This way, control over NEU policy lies directly in the hands of member states, instead of being handled by an independent European group.

Additionally, the Commission will not have 1 member for each member state, it will have 10. These members will be elected in their country of origin.

  • The European Parliament will be abolished. The duties of the Parliament will be instead passed onto the Commission, who will be able to repeal previously passed legislature or amend it as they see fit.

  • The enforcement of NEU law will be handled by governments of member states, who will be able to do as they see fit, as long as the law - which has been passed by a majority of member states - is being upheld.

  • Drafting of NEU law can be proposed by the NEU Council (which is basically all of the leaders of the member states) as well as the Commission. In this way, the organisation will act as a framework for treaties, rather than an independent governing body.

  • The European Court of Justice will be significantly scaled back. This is to reflect the changes in the structure of the NEU. Small cases will be handled either between the member states involved in a legal case, or by an intermediary member state if a decision can not be met. Larger cases will be handled by the Court of Justice with full input and co-operation from the relevant authorities of each member state.
